question: Where are DAFpay fees booked for gifts routed through the DAFpay Network (EIN 93-1372175)? Read its TY2025 Form 990 (filed 2026-05-19) Parts VIII-IX, Schedule I and Schedule O when the XML is public, and test whether the 2.9% that Chariot says applies to DPN-routed gifts appears as DPN revenue, as an expense paid to Chariot Giving Inc., or nowhere (netted before receipt). Also record DPN's self-description as a donor-advised-fund sponsor
conclusion_affected: Whether any audited filing can bound DAFpay fee leakage from DAF grants (P-AGF-02); classification of DPN as a sponsor or a pass-through
rationale: DPN's TY2024 990 shows $1.20m contributions, $831k grants, $0 program-service revenue and $18k other fees for services, while Chariot's help page says standard 2.9% DAFpay fees apply to DPN-routed gifts. DPN's mission text describes it as a sponsor of donor-advised funds. TY2025 revenue is $2.95m per ProPublica's summary, but the XML was not yet in the public S3 mirror on 2026-11-15

question: Does the Fidelity Charitable Android launch-crash cluster (5 of 12 server-rendered Play reviews, app versions 5.11-5.18, 2025-10 to 2026-08) end after the Android 5.19-5.22 releases? Re-read the public Play details page in 2027-Q1 (robots-allowed path only; no batchexecute calls) and compare with the iOS defect timeline in sponsor-app-defects-2021plus.csv
conclusion_affected: Fixable-vs-structural classification of sponsor app defects; whether Android quality lags iOS at the largest sponsor
rationale: On iOS the batch 28 sample shows no login complaint after v5.0 and a one-day hotfix for the 5.21 crash. On Android the Play sample shows five launch-crash reviews after v5.0, one saying the problem lasted months and one saying the crash blocks sign-in, on 2026 devices (Galaxy S26, Pixel 10). The Play sample is Google-selected, so recurrence needs a later re-read
